headline: Expat dies in attack during anti-drug drive in Chandpur
summary: An expatriate in Chandpur died after being attacked by local youths during an alleged anti-drug operation. He was critically injured when youths threw bricks and stones at him for questioning their activities.
details: Shahjahan Patwari, an expatriate who had returned home, died after being attacked during an alleged anti-drug operation by local youths in Chandpur Sadar. The incident occurred on Wednesday evening, August 5, in the Mandari area of Shahmahmudpur Union.

According to locals, Patwari questioned the youths who were running around during their anti-drug drive. Angered by his inquiry, the youths reportedly threw bricks and stones at him, causing severe injuries.
He was immediately rushed to the hospital, where doctors unfortunately declared him dead upon arrival. Following the tragic incident, local residents blocked a road in the Mahamaya area to protest.
Police were informed and quickly arrived at the scene to bring the situation under control. Authorities have also arrested one person suspected of involvement in the attack.

According to locals, Patwari questioned the youths who were running around during their anti-drug drive. Angered by his inquiry, the youths reportedly threw bricks and stones at him, causing severe injuries.

He was immediately rushed to the hospital, where doctors unfortunately declared him dead upon arrival. Following the tragic incident, local residents blocked a road in the Mahamaya area to protest.

Police were informed and quickly arrived at the scene to bring the situation under control. Authorities have also arrested one person suspected of involvement in the attack.

headline: Sheikh Hasina's family fled Bangladesh after government fall, while many party leaders jailed
summary: Following the government's collapse, nearly all of Sheikh Hasina's close relatives left the country to avoid arrest, contrasting with numerous Awami League leaders who are now imprisoned.
details: Former Dhaka South City Corporation Mayor Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh attempted to leave Bangladesh on August 3, 2024, but was stopped by immigration. He called Sheikh Hasina from the airport, seeking assistance to travel to Singapore.

This occurred amidst widespread student-people's protests that led to hundreds of deaths and a nationwide movement against the government. On August 3, a massive rally at Central Shaheed Minar declared a one-point demand for government resignation.

The same day, the army reportedly expressed opposition to using force against civilians, contributing to the government's unstable position. Many close relatives of Sheikh Hasina quietly left the country before and after her resignation on August 5.

These family members, who held significant power during Sheikh Hasina's 15-year rule, largely managed to avoid arrest. Most are now reportedly in India, with some seen in expensive residential buildings in Kolkata.

Sheikh Hasina herself left Bangladesh for India on August 5, 2024, accompanied by her younger sister Sheikh Rehana and defense advisor Tarique Ahmed Siddique. Sheikh Rehana, a UK permanent resident, had arrived in Dhaka two days prior.

Sheikh Hasina's son, Sajeeb Wazed Joy, was already residing in the United States before the government's fall. He was a regular visitor to Bangladesh and served as his mother's information technology advisor.

Her daughter, Saima Wazed, elected WHO's Southeast Asia regional director in November 2023, was in Delhi when the government fell. She was later sent on indefinite leave by WHO and reportedly resides between Delhi and Dubai.
Sheikh Rehana's son, Radwan Mujib Siddiq, who oversaw the Awami League's research wing, was in Thailand during the government's collapse. His wife is a Finnish citizen.
The only close relative reported arrested was Moin Uddin Abdullah, Sheikh Hasina's cousin's son, in October 2024. However, he was not politically prominent and was reportedly not in hiding.
caption:
After the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government, nearly all her close relatives fled Bangladesh to avoid arrest. This exodus contrasts sharply with numerous Awami League leaders now held in prison.

Her daughter, Saima Wazed, elected WHO's Southeast Asia regional director in November 2023, was in Delhi when the government fell. She was later sent on indefinite leave by WHO and reportedly resides between Delhi and Dubai.
